# Stock sound choices

<!-- Generated by scripts/audio/stock-sound-choices.ts from src/audio/stock-sounds.json. Do not edit by hand: change the manifest and run `npm run audio:stock-sound-choices -- render`. -->

Which recording each game sound plays, which other recordings it could
play, and which sounds are still generated. Bead `pulp_wars-2yc.24`; the
rules, the licence and the tools are in
[docs/ui/SOUND.md](../ui/SOUND.md#stock-recordings).

Nobody listened to any of these while choosing. Every choice was made
from file names and measurements, and the note beside a recording says
what was measured, not what it sounds like. That is why a sound with
more than one plausible recording keeps them all: the choice is yours.

**Since bead `pulp_wars-2yc.51` the game plays an ElevenLabs take by
default** for every sound whose takes passed their measurements
([docs/audio/ELEVENLABS_SFX.md](ELEVENLABS_SFX.md)). The recordings below
stay in the Gallery as that sound's "Old" choices, numbered as here, and
a sound's default below is what it played before the takes.

**A recording marked _your pick_ was chosen by the user by ear** (the
Rocket Cart's firework and the listening of 2026-10-14, listed in
`src/audio/sound-picks.json`). It plays by default ahead of the
ElevenLabs takes and reads "Pick" in the Gallery, first in its row; the
takes and the other recordings stay there to choose. A pick of an
ElevenLabs take is in [ELEVENLABS_SFX.md](ELEVENLABS_SFX.md).

## How to choose

1. Open the Gallery and its **Sounds** tab. A sound with recordings has a
   row under its card: your pick ("Pick") where there is one, its new
   takes ("New 1" first), its old recordings ("Old 1" is the first
   recording below; a pick keeps its number free, so the others keep
   theirs), and **Synth** last.
2. Press a line to hear it. Press **Use** on the one you like: the game
   plays it from then on, in that browser only.
3. Press **Copy my picks** at the top of the tab and paste the text to
   the developer. The default everyone gets changes only when
   `src/audio/sound-picks.json` or a manifest does.

A number below is the recording's number in that row.

## The count

- 83 game sounds.
- 11 play your pick: `attack.rocket`, `impact.rocket`, `support.rally`, `support.dark`, `cult.herald`, `cult.sacrifice`, `city.lost`, `economy.build`, `turn.end`, `ui.select`, `ui.click`.
- 32 more play a recording by default: 24 have several to choose from, 8 have one.
- 11 are generated by default and have recordings to compare with: none of those recordings is a clear match, so none replaces the generated sound until you pick it.
- 29 are generated and have no recording: the bundle has nothing that fits.
- 104 clips in the repository.

## The recordings

For each sound that has any: why these, then one line a recording. The
cut is the stretch of the original file in seconds; "level" is the
clip's `gain` in the mix.

### `attack.melee` — Melee swing

Recorded — 2 options awaiting your pick. The Melee Weapons library has no swing or whoosh, only scrapes, drops and hits. A slow sword scrape is the nearest thing to a blade in motion; the anime library's sword cut is the only designed sword sound of the bundle.

| #         | Default | Part | Library / original file                                                                   | Cut         | Level | What was measured                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------- | ------- | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1         | yes     | 2    | Justsoundeffects - Melee Weapons / `WEAPSwrd_Weapon 03 Slow Scrapes_JSE_MW.wav`           | 16.93–17.38 | 0.45  | A metal scrape that swells for 150 ms and rings out, around 5 kHz; 0.45 s. The eighth of ten scrapes (16.89 to 17.54 s), the one with the quickest rise.                                                  |
| 2         |         | 6    | Rogue Waves - Anime Studio / `WEAPSwrd_Mecha Energy Sword Cut_RogueWaves_AnimeStudio.wav` | 0.06–0.45   | 0.7   | A sharp attack and a tone that climbs from 1.5 to 2.4 kHz in 150 ms: a designed 'shing', more science fiction; 0.39 s. The cut itself (it starts at 0.08 s), without the low tail that follows to 1.05 s. |
| Generated |         |      | The synthesised sound                                                                     |             |       | Always there: it plays until a clip has loaded, and it can be picked.                                                                                                                                     |

### `attack.ray` — Energy ray

Recorded — 2 options awaiting your pick. The Martian ray wants a cartoon laser. The anime laser beam is named for it; the science-fiction 'zap' is the only other short energy sound whose energy is not all below 150 Hz.

| #         | Default | Part | Library / original file                                         | Cut   | Level | What was measured                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------- | ------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1         | yes     | 1    | Doex Studio - 90s Anime SFX Pack / `Laser_Beam_004.wav`         | 0–0.5 | 0.55  | A burst at 0.8 to 1.5 kHz for 200 ms, then a low body around 300 Hz; 0.5 s. The first of three identical takes; its opening burst, without the two-second low tail. |
| 2         |         | 6    | Rescopic Sound - Parallax / `SCIMisc_Zap Short 14_RSCPC_PX.wav` | 0–0.5 | 0.5   | A broad noisy crackle centred near 1.1 kHz, no clear pitch, steadier and rougher than the laser; 0.5 s. The first half second of a 1.9 s zap, faded out.            |
| Generated |         |      | The synthesised sound                                           |       |       | Always there: it plays until a clip has loaded, and it can be picked.                                                                                               |

### `attack.rocket` — Rocket launch

Recorded — your pick. A flare leaving its tube for the Rocket Cart's firework. Since 2026-10-14 the user's pick by ear: an RPG fired at a car, whose launch is this sound and whose impact is `impact.rocket`.

| #         | Default   | Part | Library / original file                                                                                           | Cut         | Level | What was measured                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | --------- | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1         | yes       | 1    | BluezoneCorp - Steampunk Weapon And Textures / `Bluezone_BC0296_steampunk_weapon_flare_shot_explosion_003.wav`    | 0–0.5       | 0.45  | A noisy launch at 1 to 3 kHz for a quarter of a second; 0.5 s. The flare shot (the first event, 0 to 0.64 s), without the burst that follows at 0.84 s.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
